about.an-independent-nonpartisan-record-: An independent, nonpartisan record of what was announced at each polling unit — documented, verified and published by ordinary Nigerians.
about.elections-are-won-at-the-polling: Elections are won at the polling unit, then at collation. When numbers can change on the way up, trust collapses. So every report here is photographed, signed on the observer's own phone and chained on a public ledger — and a count is trusted only when independent observers at the same place agree, backed by GPS and matching venue photos.
about.hawkeye-does-not-declare-winners-a: Hawkeye does not declare winners, and its tallies are not official results — those come only from INEC. It is a record built to aid scrutiny, unaffiliated with INEC, any party, candidate or campaign.

captain-guide.invite-1: Your own invite link is in My Profile, under Invite. Share it on WhatsApp or by text. Each person who signs up with it shows on your profile.
captain-guide.invite-2: For groups and notice boards, share the Get Hawkeye page.
captain-guide.invite-3: Each volunteer saves their own polling unit in the app. Never collect a list of who is going where.
captain-guide.lede: A ward captain makes sure someone stays for the count at every polling unit in one ward. You are a volunteer, and Hawkeye stays independent of every party.
captain-guide.never-1: It never shares who watches which polling unit — not with you, not with a party, not with anyone.
captain-guide.never-2: It never publishes coverage below local government level.
captain-guide.never-3: Being a captain gives you no access to anyone's details in the app.
captain-guide.rules-1: Recruit anyone, from any party or none. Party agents are welcome on the same terms as everyone else.
captain-guide.rules-2: No party names, logos, colours or slogans in anything you send about Hawkeye.
captain-guide.rules-3: Say "record what is announced". Never promise to expose rigging, and never predict a winner.
captain-guide.rules-4: Hawkeye is not INEC and not a party. Say so first.
captain-guide.rules-5: Never offer money or gifts for joining or reporting.
captain-guide.safety-1: No result is worth your life. If there is trouble, leave, and report it later from somewhere safe.
captain-guide.safety-2: Never interfere with election officials, voters or materials. Follow officials' instructions.
captain-guide.safety-3: Follow the Electoral Act and INEC's rules. Photograph only what is posted or handed out.

cert.q1: When do you photograph the result sheet (EC8A)?
cert.q1-a: As soon as you arrive at the polling unit
cert.q1-b: When the result is announced and posted after the count
cert.q1-c: Later, from a picture someone sends you
cert.q1-why: Stay for the count. The presiding officer counts the ballots in public and fills in the EC8A; the announcement is the moment that matters. Photograph only what is posted or handed out.
cert.q2: Can you report with a photo from your gallery, or a screenshot?
cert.q2-a: No. Photos are taken live in the app, at the unit
cert.q2-b: Yes, if the photo is clear
cert.q2-c: Yes, if a friend at the unit sent it
cert.q2-why: Live photos only: no gallery uploads, no screenshots. Each photo is GPS-stamped when it is taken, which makes a report hard to fake from somewhere else.
cert.q3: What do you type into your report?
cert.q3-a: Your own estimate of the votes
cert.q3-b: The figures someone at the unit tells you
cert.q3-c: Each party’s figure exactly as announced
cert.q3-why: Type each party’s announced figure exactly, then sign and submit while you are still at the unit. Reports are permanent: nothing can be edited or deleted after signing.
cert.q4: How should you treat election officials, voters and materials?
cert.q4-a: Never interfere, and follow officials’ instructions
cert.q4-b: Step in if you think an official made a mistake
cert.q4-why: Never interfere with election officials, voters or materials. Follow officials’ instructions, and follow the Electoral Act and INEC’s rules.
cert.q5: Trouble breaks out at your polling unit. What do you do?
cert.q5-a: Stay and keep photographing, whatever happens
cert.q5-b: Leave, and report it later from somewhere safe
cert.q5-why: No result is worth your life. If there is trouble, leave, and report it later from somewhere safe.
cert.q6-a: As soon as one observer reports it
cert.q6-b: When it is shared widely online
cert.q6-c: When independent observers at the same unit report matching numbers
cert.q6-why: No single report is trusted on its own. A count is verified when independent observers at the same unit report matching numbers, backed by GPS, matching venue photos and the digits read from the sheet. Hawkeye does not declare results: official results are INEC’s.
cert.q7-a: The count reported at a polling unit
cert.q7-b: Your phone number, or who watches which polling unit
cert.q7-why: Your phone number is hashed and never published or shared. Hawkeye never shares who watches which polling unit: not with a captain, not with a party, not with anyone.

faq.no-hawkeye-is-an-independent-communi: No. Hawkeye is an independent, community-run transparency initiative. The tallies shown here are crowd-verified evidence of what was announced at individual polling units — the official results of any election are only those declared by INEC.

guide.type-each-party-s-announced-figure: Type each party's announced figure exactly, then sign and submit while still at the unit. Photos expire if you wait, and your GPS must match where the photos were taken. Several elections may be counted at your unit the same day — submit one report per election, each with its own photos.
guide.voting-ends-then-the-presiding-off: Voting ends, then the presiding officer counts ballots publicly and fills in the EC8A result sheet for each election. This — the announcement — is the moment that matters.
how.a-ledger-nobody-can-quietly-edit: ⛓️ A ledger nobody can quietly edit
how.a-verified-phone-number-is-one: A verified phone number is one observer identity. Numbers are stored only as one-way hashes — never readable, never published.
how.each-photo-is-gps-stamped-at: Each photo is GPS-stamped at capture; the sheet, venue and submission positions must all agree, and photos expire within minutes.
how.each-report-is-signed-on-the: Each report is signed on the observer's phone with a key that never leaves it, then chained to the previous entry by cryptographic hash.
how.each-report-is-tagged-to-its: Each report is tagged to its races automatically — state, senatorial district and federal constituency come from the official register.
how.every-unit-also-has-an-approximate: Every unit also has an approximate area from open geographic data; reports or mapping fixes far outside it are rejected outright.
how.follow-any-race-everywhere-or-a-sing: Follow any race — everywhere, or a single state, district or constituency — and Hawkeye pings you in the app whenever new reports land. Subscribe on the results page. Race alerts also post in our Telegram channel, @HawkeyeNG_Results.
how.hawkeye-turns-thousands-of-ordinary-: Hawkeye turns thousands of ordinary phones into a network of independent witnesses. No single report is trusted on its own — trust is earned when separate people, provably at the same place, say the same thing.
how.map-your-unit-before-election-day: Map Your Unit Before Election Day
how.most-polling-units-have-no-verified: Most polling units have no verified GPS location. Stand at yours and pin it before the vote.
how.photos-are-captured-live-in-the: Photos are captured live in the app — the EC8A sheet is auto-detected, flattened and quality-checked (blur/glare) like a document scanner.
how.re-submitting-someone-else-s-photo: Re-submitting someone else's photo — or a near-identical copy — is detected and rejected by image fingerprinting.
how.tap-each-layer-to-see-how: Tap each layer to see how it works.
how.the-typed-counts-are-cross-checked: The typed counts are cross-checked against the digits machine-read from the sheet photograph itself.
how.units-without-one-accept-reports-but: Units without one accept reports, but the count stays visibly "location-unverified" until at least three independent observers' GPS positions cluster at the same spot.
how.venue-photos-from-different-observer: Venue photos from different observers are feature-matched to confirm they stood at the same physical place.
how.verify-your-phone-then-photograph-th: Verify your phone, then photograph the announced EC8A results sheet and the venue on election day. Your report is signed on your device and recorded permanently.
how.watch-the-leaderboard-live-and-subsc: Watch the leaderboard live, and subscribe to alerts for the presidential race, your state, senatorial district or constituency.

press.step-1: Photograph the sheet. At the polling unit, an observer photographs the announced result sheet and the venue in the app. Photos are taken live and GPS-stamped; gallery uploads are not accepted.
press.step-2: Sign and record. The report is signed on the observer's own phone, with a key Hawkeye never holds, and added to a public record that cannot be quietly edited.
press.step-3: Compare in the open. Reports from the same unit are compared with each other and with INEC's own sheet on IReV. A count is marked verified only when independent observers agree, and a disagreement is shown, never hidden.
press.summary: Hawkeye is a free, open-source app that lets any Nigerian at a polling unit photograph the result sheet (Form EC8A) announced there and add it to a public record anyone can check. Reports from the same unit are compared with each other and with the copy INEC uploads to its IReV portal, so agreement, or a mismatch, is visible to all. Hawkeye is independent and nonpartisan: it does not declare results, it is not a rival count, and it is not affiliated with INEC or any party or candidate.
press.trust-ledger: Public ledger. Every report is chained to the one before it, and the ledger's fingerprint is published in Sigstore Rekor, an independent public log Hawkeye does not run. Anyone can re-check it in the browser, with no account.
press.trust-nonpartisan: Nonpartisan. Hawkeye declares no winners and backs no party or candidate. It takes no political money and carries no advertising.
press.trust-open: Open source. The code is public on GitHub, and the open verifier lets anyone re-check the record with their own tools.
press.trust-photos: Photo privacy. Result sheets are public, as INEC posts them at the unit. Photos of the venue, which can show voters, are never published. Phone numbers are stored only as one-way hashes.

STAY FOR THE COUNT – Saturday 16 January 2027

Hawkeye is a free app for Nigerians. It is independent and nonpartisan: not INEC, not the government, not a political party.

Before 16 January:
1. Install Hawkeye Election Monitor or Hawkeye Lite (Google Play or App Store)
2. Verify your number
3. Save your polling unit
4. Do the free practice run

On the day: vote, then stay for the count or come back. When the result is posted, photograph it in Hawkeye and submit. It becomes part of a public record anyone can check. No signal? It sends later.

No result is worth your life. Follow officials' instructions. Never interfere or argue. Photograph only what is posted or handed out.

tgbroadcast.admin.refused-sent: This message was already sent. Check the last broadcast below; type SEND again only if you mean to send it twice.
tgbroadcast.admin.resumed: Resumed: {posts} channel posts and {dms} direct messages.
tgbroadcast.admin.started: Started: {posts} channel posts and {dms} direct messages.
tgbroadcast.admin.target-channels: Post to our Telegram channels, each language to its own channel
tgbroadcast.admin.target-followers: Also message race-alert followers directly, each in their language, paced, once per broadcast
tgbroadcast.admin.title: Telegram broadcast
tgbroadcast.admin.waiting-note: {waiting} followers have not had it (for example, people who blocked the bot, or who followed since). Resume retries only them.
tgnotice.admin.done: Last send finished: {sent} of {audience} sent, {failed} failed.
tgnotice.admin.failed-note: Chats that failed (for example, people who blocked the bot) are still waiting. Sending again retries only them.
tgnotice.admin.interrupted: Last send stopped after {sent} of {audience} because the server restarted. Send again to reach the rest. Nobody gets it twice.
tgnotice.admin.intro: One direct message to everyone who follows a race on Telegram, saying race alerts have moved to our channel. Each chat gets it once, ever. Nothing is sent until you type SEND and press Send notice.
tgnotice.admin.no-run: Not sent from the console yet.
tgnotice.admin.not-live: Channel alerts are not live, so the notice cannot be sent. It needs the channels set, channel alerts switched on, the bot token and the channel strings.
tgnotice.admin.nothing: Nobody is waiting for the notice.
tgnotice.admin.rate-limited: Too many console requests. Try again in {s} seconds.
tgnotice.admin.reason-nobody: Nobody is waiting for this notice.
tgnotice.admin.reason-not-live: Channel alerts are not live, so the notice cannot be sent.
tgnotice.admin.refused-confirm: Type SEND exactly, in capital letters.
tgnotice.admin.refused-max: Refresh the preview, then send again.
tgnotice.admin.refused-more: More chats are waiting than the preview showed ({audience}, not {max}). Check the new numbers, then send again.
tgnotice.admin.run-failed: Last send stopped with an error after {sent} of {audience} ({error}).
tgnotice.admin.running: Sending: {sent} of {audience} sent, {failed} failed. You can close this page; the server keeps going.
tgnotice.admin.title: Telegram channel notice
tgnotice.admin.unconfirmed: In flight when the server stopped: {n}. They are not sent again, so they may not have arrived.

video-player.failed: This video could not be played. Check your connection and try again.
